items.title: PIX2DB: Reconstructing Executable Relational Databases from Document Images with a 2B Vision-Language Model
items.summary: Abstract Tables trapped in screenshots, scans, receipts and charts are usually extracted as markup that keeps the layout but not the relational meaning: merged cells stay merged, an invoice header and its line items stay unrelated, and “$1,250.00” stays a string. We study image-to-database reconstruction: given one image, produce a SQLite dump whose schema, column types, keys and rows load and can be queried as they are. Training data with exact gold databases is obtained in two ways: by rendering samples of the Spider databases at six layout levels, and by converting PubTabNet, FinTabNet and CORD annotations under the same normalization rules. A 2B model (Qwen3-VL-2B with LoRA) trained on 36,589 pairs and followed by a deterministic verify-and-repair layer reaches 0.86 table exact match and 0.99 foreign-key recall on rendered tables from unseen databases, against 0.75/0.75 for the 8B model of the same family prompted for SQL and 0.47/0.00 for an 8B HTML-to-SQLite pipeline. On held-out real images it obtains cell F1 0.81 (PubTabNet) and 0.96 (FinTabNet) and recall 0.93 on CORD receipt photos. On TabRecSet, a source not used in training, it is the best system that writes a database directly (0.52) but trails the 8B HTML pipeline (0.58), mostly in reading text from photographs. items.title: Differential diagnosis of pulmonary Talaromyces marneffei infection and pulmonary tuberculosis in HIV/AIDS patients using a CT-based multimodal 2.5D deep learning approach
items.summary: Background To investigate the diagnostic value of a computed tomography (CT)-based multimodal 2.5-dimensional (2.5D) deep learning model for differentiating Talaromyces marneffei (TSM) from pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) in patients with human immunodeficiency virus infection/acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (HIV/AIDS). Methods A total of 380 HIV/AIDS patients with pulmonary infections who were admitted to the Fourth People’s Hospital of Nanning from January 2018 to August 2025 were retrospectively enrolled, including 203 patients with PTB, 177 with TSM. The cohort was randomly divided into a training set and a test set at a ratio of 7:3. A clinical model, a radiomics model, and a 2.5D deep learning model were constructed separately. Results In the clinical feature model, Random Forest achieved the optimal performance, with a test set AUC of 0.856. In the radiomics model, XGBoost attained the highest AUC of 0.866. In the 2.5D deep learning model, ResNet18 performed best at the slice level with an AUC of 0.865, and the patient-level support vector machine (SVM) model based on MIL achieved an AUC of 0.885. The multimodal combined model integrating clinical, radiomics, and deep learning features achieved the highest AUC of 0.931 and a specificity of 0.981. items.title: Generative AI in Second Language Video Composing: Investigating Students' Critical Digital Literacies and Multimodal Redesign
items.summary: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in digital multimodal composing (DMC) presents both opportunities and challenges for second language (L2) research and pedagogy. While GenAI tools provide linguistic and multimodal support, they also raise concerns about biased information, culturally generic outputs, and technological overreliance. This qualitative study investigates L2 students' enactment of critical digital literacies (CDL) during GenAI‐assisted video composing. Drawing on CDL as a theoretical orientation and the analytical heuristic of critical awareness, critical identities, critical relationships, and critical actions, the study examines how students negotiated and revised AI‐generated video representations. Using multimodal critical discourse analysis of screen recordings, final video artifacts, focus group interviews, and reflective essays from 20 L2 students, the findings reveal four interrelated forms of CDL enactment. Students demonstrated critical awareness of GenAI's culturally limited outputs, authored critical identities through multimodal redesign, negotiated critical relationships with peers and GenAI, and engaged in localized critical action against cultural erasure. However, students' varied responses also highlight the uneven opportunities for CDL enactment across student groups. These findings offer theoretical and pedagogical implications

items.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
items.summary: Video foundation models have advanced rapidly in understanding and generating visual sequences, while video world models seek to capture the underlying dynamics of the world they depict. Despite their different objectives, both concern the relationship between video observations and an evolving world. This survey adopts world modeling as a unifying lens for examining these developments. Viewing an observed video as a partial, lossy, and temporally ordered projection of a latent temporal world, we organize the literature around four complementary operations: reading infers world properties from observed video; writing synthesizes video from specified or learned world conditions; sharing integrates understanding and generation through common modeling mechanisms; and interacting predicts and updates world states under actions and evolving observations. This perspective distinguishes temporal coherence in observed or generated sequences from consistency in the underlying world state. Across tasks, representations, models, datasets, and benchmarks, we trace a shift in emphasis from clip-level recognition and perceptual fidelity toward persistent state, controllable evolution, physical and causal validity, and evaluation grounded in interaction and downstream decisions, and we distill the open challenges that follow.

items.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
items.summary: Auditing whether a text-to-image (T2I) model was fine-tuned on a particular image collection is difficult: a model can absorb collection-level visual characteristics without reproducing training images. Proactive dataset-use auditing plants a shared signal in a dataset before release, then later checks whether that signal appears in a suspect model's generated outputs. Existing approaches often trade off verifiability, fidelity, robustness, and deployability. We introduce $\textbf{SpectralCanary}$, which uses a smooth low-pass mask to blend a fixed canary image into every collection image while leaving captions unchanged and requiring neither auxiliary generation nor per-image optimization. A lightweight verifier detects the transferred signal in suspect-model outputs. Across eight tests on the Pokemon dataset and three realistic data transformations, spanning two architectures families, SpectralCanary achieves the highest average per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR ($91.1\%$) and fixed threshold model-level accuracy using 30 generations ($94.8\%$) among the evaluated methods. Across five datasets spanning artistic, medical, satellite, and fashion domains with SD3.5, SpectralCanary averages $92.4\%$ per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR while preserving the released images (SSIM $0.989$, LPIPS $0.022$) with a near-zero mean change FID (mean $Δ$FID $0.05$) across datasets.
